name: Residential Roofing
title: Residential Roofing in Dallas–Fort Worth | Timber Roofing
description: Residential roofing for DFW and North Texas homes — replacements, repairs, and inspections handled by licensed inspectors. Free inspections and free estimates.
heroSub: The roof is the one part of your house that works every single day and gets looked at almost never. We look at it properly, tell you what we find, and do the work right.
intro: Most North Texas homes are covered in architectural asphalt shingles, and most of them will need attention somewhere between year twelve and year twenty-five. Hail moves that timeline. So does poor ventilation, a bad original install, or a decade of 100-degree Augusts baking the granules off the south-facing slopes.

We work on single-family homes across Dallas–Fort Worth and the surrounding communities — from 1970s ranch houses in Richardson and Garland to the steep, cut-up rooflines that came with the Frisco and Prosper build-out. Different eras, different problems. A licensed inspector looks at yours before anybody quotes a number.

signs.d: Shingles shed their protective surface as they age. A handful of granules after a new install is normal. Piles of them in year fifteen are not.
Water rarely enters directly above the stain. It travels. That is why the source has to be found from the roof and the attic, not guessed from below.

signs.t: Shingles that look bruised or dented
signs.d: Hail impact often shows as soft dark circles where granules were knocked loose rather than obvious holes.
Usually heat and age, sometimes a ventilation problem underneath. Either way the seal strip is no longer doing its job in high wind.

signs.t: A roof that is simply old
signs.d: If you have no idea how old it is and you have lived there a while, that by itself is worth a free inspection.

causes.d: North Texas sits in one of the most active hail corridors in the country. Impact damage is the single most common reason a DFW roof gets replaced early.
Straight-line winds ahead of a squall line break shingle seals and peel edges, especially on the windward slope and along rakes and ridges.
Surface temperatures on a dark shingle roof in a Texas July are brutal, and the daily expansion and contraction ages the mat and the sealant.
Under-ventilated attics cook shingles from below and shorten their service life from the side you cannot see.
Over-driven nails, missing starter course, skipped ice-and-water at valleys, reused flashing. We find all of it, most often on a roof somebody else put on cheap.

inspection: Walk the roof where it is safe to do so, and use drone imagery where it is not
Check field shingles, ridge caps, valleys, rakes, eaves, and every penetration
Look at flashing at walls, chimneys, skylights, and pipe boots
Check gutters and downspouts for granule load and drainage problems
Go into the attic where accessible to look for daylight, staining, and ventilation
Photograph everything and walk you through the photos in plain language

process.d: A licensed inspector assesses the roof and documents condition with photos.
We show you what we found and explain what is urgent, what can wait, and what is cosmetic.
Free, itemized, and yours to keep. Repair and replacement options where both are legitimate.
Nothing is ordered or scheduled until you approve the scope in writing.
Materials delivered, property protected, tear-off and install handled by our crew.
Magnet sweep for nails, debris hauled, and a final walkthrough with you before we leave.

options.d: The default for good reason in this market — strong wind ratings, deep shadow lines, and a wide color range that suits North Texas brick.
Class 4 rated products are worth a conversation in a hail corridor. Ask us what the real-world trade-offs are before you assume they are always the answer.
Still found on older rentals and smaller structures. We will install them where they make sense and tell you when they do not.
Synthetic underlayment, ice-and-water membrane in valleys and around penetrations, new pipe boots, new flashing, and proper ridge ventilation.
Balanced intake and exhaust addressed as part of the roof rather than treated as a separate trade.
New step, counter, and apron flashing plus fresh boots on every vent, rather than reusing what is there.

benefits: A licensed inspector, not a salesperson, assesses your roof
Photo documentation you keep whether or not you hire us
Repair recommended when repair is genuinely the right call
Your driveway, landscaping, and windows protected during the work
Nails swept, debris hauled, and a walkthrough before we call it done
localNote: North Texas asks a lot of a roof: hail in spring, straight-line wind ahead of the storms, then four months of relentless heat. A roof system that would last twenty-five years in a mild climate often does not get there here, and the failure usually starts at the details — valleys, flashing, boots, and ventilation — rather than in the middle of the field.

faqs.q: How long does a roof last in Dallas–Fort Worth?
faqs.a: Architectural asphalt shingles are commonly rated well past twenty years, but North Texas hail and heat frequently shorten the real service life. Age alone does not decide it — condition does. That is what the inspection is for.

faqs.q: Do I need a full replacement or can it be repaired?
faqs.a: It depends on how widespread the damage is, how old the roof is, and whether matching material is realistic. If a repair will genuinely hold, we will tell you that. We would rather do a good repair now than sell a replacement you did not need.

faqs.q: Is the inspection really free?
faqs.a: Yes. Free inspections and free estimates, with no obligation to schedule work.

faqs.q: How long does a residential roof replacement take?
faqs.a: Many single-family homes are a one to two day job once materials are on site, depending on size, pitch, complexity, and weather. We will give you a realistic window with your estimate.

faqs.q: Will you work on my house if I am outside the Metroplex?
faqs.a: Often, yes. We regularly work across North Texas and travel roughly two hours from Dallas for the right project. Call with your address and we will give you a straight answer.

name: Roof Replacement
title: Roof Replacement in DFW & North Texas | Timber Roofing
description: Full roof replacement for North Texas homes — tear-off, deck inspection, new underlayment, flashing, and shingles. Free inspection and a free written estimate.
heroSub: Tear off, look at the deck, fix what is under there, and build the system back correctly. A replacement is only as good as the parts nobody sees.
intro: A replacement is not just new shingles. It is a system: decking, underlayment, ice-and-water protection at the vulnerable spots, drip edge, valley treatment, flashing, penetration boots, ventilation, and then the shingles on top. Skip any one of those and the roof will tell on itself in a few years.

The most useful moment of any replacement is the hour after tear-off, when the deck is exposed. Soft plywood, old leaks, rot around a chimney, or a previous repair done badly — that is when it becomes visible. We photograph it and talk to you before we cover it back up.

signs.d: When impact damage is spread across multiple slopes rather than concentrated in one area, spot repair stops making sense.
One leak is an event. Three leaks in three seasons is a roof telling you it is finished.

signs.t: Bare or heavily worn shingle mat
signs.d: Once granule loss exposes the asphalt, UV goes to work on the mat directly and the countdown accelerates.
A visible dip usually means the structure or the deck underneath has taken on moisture.
Sometimes repair is technically fine but a color match is impossible, and the decision becomes an appearance question.

causes.d: Several seasons of hail and wind stack up, and a roof that survived each individual storm reaches the end together.
Sun does the slow work. South and west-facing slopes almost always age first in Texas.
Nailing above the line, missing starter strip, or no valley protection will cut years off an otherwise good product.
Superheated attic air degrades shingles from underneath and can void material coverage.

inspection: Full condition assessment by a licensed inspector, documented with photos
Slope-by-slope evaluation so damage patterns are recorded accurately
Penetration, flashing, and valley review — these decide most replacements
Attic check for ventilation, moisture, and deck condition where accessible
Measurement and material takeoff for an itemized written estimate

process.d: Free inspection, photo documentation, and a written itemized estimate with material and color options.
You approve the scope. We order material and schedule around the weather window.
Tarps and protection over landscaping, windows, AC units, and the driveway before anything comes off.
Old roofing removed to the deck. Anything soft, rotted, or damaged is documented and shown to you.
Underlayment, ice-and-water at valleys and penetrations, drip edge, new flashing, new boots, shingles, ridge, and ventilation.
Magnet sweep, debris hauled off, gutters cleared of tear-off debris, and a walkthrough with you.

options.d: Dimensional profile, strong wind performance, and the widest color selection. The standard choice for most North Texas homes.
Built to better tolerate hail impact. Worth discussing here given the hail corridor — we will explain the real trade-offs rather than upsell you.
Ridge vents, static vents, or turbines matched to your attic intake so the new roof breathes properly.
Replacement of damaged or rotted sheathing, priced transparently and only where it is actually needed.
Across the whole deck, tear-resistant and stable underfoot if weather arrives mid-job.
Self-adhering protection in valleys and around penetrations, where the volume actually concentrates.

benefits: The deck gets inspected while it is open, not covered up
New flashing and boots rather than reusing tired ones
Ventilation addressed as part of the system, not as an afterthought
Itemized written estimate before anything is ordered
Nail sweep and haul-off included, not an extra line item
localNote: Replacements cluster in North Texas after spring hail season, which means the busiest crews in the Metroplex are often the least careful ones. A replacement scheduled properly, with the deck actually inspected and the flashing actually replaced, is worth waiting a few days for.

faqs.q: Can you roof over the existing shingles?
faqs.a: We do not recommend it. A layover hides deck problems, adds weight, traps heat, and makes the next replacement more expensive. Tear-off is how you find out what is really under there.

faqs.q: What happens if you find rotted decking?
faqs.a: We stop, photograph it, show you, and price the repair before we proceed. You will not get a surprise line item after the fact.

faqs.q: How much noise and disruption should I expect?
faqs.a: Tear-off day is genuinely loud, and things on shelves can vibrate. Most homeowners find it easiest to plan around it, especially with small children or anyone working from home.

faqs.q: Do I need to be home during the work?
faqs.a: Not usually, though we like you there for the final walkthrough. We will keep you updated either way.

faqs.q: What about my landscaping and driveway?
faqs.a: They get protected before tear-off starts, and we run magnets over the yard, beds, and drive at the end. Nails in tires are the most common complaint about roofing crews, and it is entirely preventable.

name: Roof Repair
title: Roof Repair in Dallas–Fort Worth | Timber Roofing
description: Roof repair across DFW and North Texas — leaks, missing shingles, flashing, valleys, and pipe boots. Free inspection and honest repair-or-replace advice.
h1: Roof Repair, Diagnosed Before It Is Priced
heroSub: Plenty of roofs get replaced that only needed a repair. We will tell you which one you have.
intro: A good repair starts with finding the actual source rather than the nearest suspicious-looking shingle. Water gets in at a flashing detail or a failed boot, runs along a rafter, and shows up on a ceiling ten feet away. Patching where the stain is fixes nothing.

We repair what can be repaired. If your roof has plenty of life left and the problem is confined, a proper repair is the right answer and we will say so — even though a replacement would be the bigger invoice.

signs.t: A stain that grows after rain
signs.d: Active intrusion. Worth looking at before the drywall and insulation are involved.
Common after a wind event. The exposed area underneath is on borrowed time.
Rubber boots around plumbing vents are one of the most frequent leak sources on a Texas roof, and one of the cheapest to fix.
Where the roof meets a wall, chimney, or skylight is where roofs actually leak.

causes.d: Boots, vents, and satellite mounts degrade in UV long before the shingles do.
Once a seal strip breaks, the shingle no longer bonds and the next storm takes it.
Valleys carry the most water on the roof and wear out first, especially where two large planes converge.
Sealant smeared over a flashing problem is a delay tactic, not a repair, and we find a lot of it.

inspection: Trace the leak from the interior evidence back to the actual entry point
Inspect all penetrations, flashing, valleys, and transitions
Check the surrounding field for hidden damage that would make the repair pointless
Assess remaining roof life so you can weigh repair against replacement honestly
Photograph the failure point so you can see the problem yourself

process.d: We find the source and document it.
Repair, replace, or monitor — with reasoning, not pressure.
Scoped to the actual repair, itemized, free.
Materials matched as closely as available, flashing replaced rather than resealed where appropriate.
Work reviewed, area cleaned, and photos of the completed repair.
We look at the repair again after the next real rain if you want us to, rather than assuming it held.

options.d: Replacing damaged shingles and re-establishing the seal correctly rather than face-nailing them down.
New step, counter, or apron flashing at walls and chimneys. Sealant alone is a temporary measure at best.
New boots on plumbing vents, often the highest-value small repair on the roof.
Stripping back and rebuilding the valley with proper membrane and layering.
Rebuilding the flashing kit around a skylight, which is a far more common leak source than the unit itself.
Replacing sheathing that has already softened under a chronic leak, so the new work has something solid to sit on.

benefits: Diagnosis first, so you are paying to fix the real problem
An honest repair-versus-replace answer, in writing
Photos of the failure point and of the completed repair
Small repairs treated as real work, not as a nuisance job
localNote: In North Texas the same repair shows up over and over: a cracked pipe boot on a south-facing slope, wind-lifted shingles on the windward rake, and old chimney flashing that was sealed instead of replaced. None of those require a new roof — they require somebody willing to do a small job well.

faqs.q: Will the repair match my existing shingles?
faqs.a: We match as closely as the product line allows. Weathering means a repair on an older roof is usually visible on close inspection, and we will be upfront about that before we start.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing an older roof?
faqs.a: Sometimes, absolutely. If the roof is otherwise sound and the damage is confined, a repair can buy you real years. If it is failing in several places at once, repair money is wasted money and we will say so.

faqs.q: How quickly can you get out for an active leak?
faqs.a: Call us. Active water intrusion moves to the front of the line, and we will tell you honestly when we can be there rather than promising a time we cannot hold.

faqs.q: Can a small leak really cause much damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Chronic slow leaks wet insulation, rot decking, and feed mold in a hot attic, and the repair bill for what the water touched routinely exceeds the roofing repair itself.

intro: An inspection is not a sales visit with a ladder. It is a documented assessment of a roof system: field condition, penetrations, flashing, valleys, drainage, and ventilation, recorded with photographs so you can see what we saw.

Our inspections are performed by licensed inspectors. If your roof is fine, we will tell you it is fine and leave you with the report. That is not a hard business decision — it is the only version of this job worth doing.

signs.t: After any significant hail or wind event
signs.d: Damage is frequently invisible from the ground and does not always leak right away.

signs.t: Before buying or selling a home
signs.d: Roof condition moves negotiations more than almost any other single item.

signs.t: When you do not know the roof's age
signs.d: Very common for homes bought secondhand. A baseline is worth having.
Regular checks catch small failures while they are still small.

causes.d: Hail bruising and lifted seals are hard to see from the ground and easy to miss from a driveway estimate.
One cracked boot becomes wet insulation, then a stained ceiling, then a decking repair.
Dated photographs of roof condition are useful to have on file long before you need them.

inspection: Exterior walk of the roof where safe, with drone imagery for steep or fragile sections
Slope-by-slope documentation of field condition and damage patterns
Close review of flashing, valleys, penetrations, ridge, rakes, and eaves
Gutter and drainage check, including granule accumulation
Attic review where accessible for daylight, staining, and ventilation performance
Photo set plus a plain-language walkthrough of the findings

process.d: Call or send the form. We confirm a window that works for you.
A licensed inspector evaluates the roof and attic and documents condition.
We show you the photos and explain what is urgent, what to watch, and what is fine.
If work is needed, you get a free written estimate. If it is not, you get told that.
Where there is safe access, we check for daylight, staining, insulation condition, and whether the ventilation is actually moving air.
Free and itemized if the roof needs work. If it does not, you get told that instead.

options.d: Focused on impact and wind damage patterns after a specific weather event.
A baseline read on remaining service life for planning and budgeting.
Documented roof condition ahead of a sale or purchase.
Targeted diagnosis when there is active water intrusion.
A yearly baseline so you have a documented history rather than a single snapshot.
Dated photographs and a written roofing scope you may share with your carrier at your discretion.

benefits: Performed by licensed inspectors
Free, with no obligation and no pressure
You keep the photographs and the findings
Drone imagery for areas that should not be walked
Clear language instead of a scare tactic
localNote: The Metroplex sees hail somewhere across the region most spring seasons, and damage is highly localized — one street gets hit while the next one over does not. That is exactly why a ground-level guess is worth so little and why a documented inspection after a storm is worth the hour.

faqs.q: What does the inspection cost?
faqs.a: Nothing. Free inspections and free estimates.

faqs.q: Do I get a written report?
faqs.a: You get the photo documentation and a clear walkthrough of the findings, plus a free written estimate if work is recommended.

faqs.q: Do you walk the roof or fly it?
faqs.a: Both, depending on pitch, height, material, and safety. Some roofs should not be walked, and drone imagery gives a better record anyway.

faqs.q: Will you tell me my roof is fine if it is fine?
faqs.a: Yes. Plenty of inspections end with no work needed.

faqs.q: How long does an inspection take?
faqs.a: Usually under an hour for a typical single-family home, longer for large or complex rooflines.

name: Asphalt Shingle Roofing
title: Asphalt Shingle Roofing in Texas | Timber Roofing
description: Architectural and impact-resistant asphalt shingle roofing installed across DFW. Material guidance, color selection, and free written estimates.
h1: Asphalt Shingle Roofing for Texas Homes
heroSub: The right shingle for a hail corridor with 100-degree summers is a different conversation than the one they have in Oregon.
intro: Asphalt shingles cover the overwhelming majority of homes in North Texas, and for good reason: strong wind performance, sane cost, wide color range, and repairability. The differences that matter here are impact rating, weight, wind rating, and how the product handles sustained heat.

Color is not only an appearance decision in this climate. Darker roofs run hotter, and attic ventilation has to keep up either way. We will walk you through the options against your brick, your trim, and any HOA requirements.

signs.t: You are choosing a replacement product
signs.d: This is the decision that determines how the roof performs for the next two decades.
Older three-tab roofs are common on North Texas homes built before the 2000s and generally underperform modern architectural products in wind.
Worth a real conversation in this region, including the trade-offs nobody mentions.

causes.d: Sustained high surface temperatures age the asphalt mat and soften sealant bonds.
Granule loss and mat bruising are the standard failure mode in this market.
Wind rating and correct nailing pattern matter more than most homeowners are told.

inspection: Confirm existing shingle type, layer count, and condition
Assess deck and ventilation before recommending a product
Review color options against the home's brick, stone, and trim
Check any HOA or neighborhood requirements you are aware of

process.d: We narrow the field to products that make sense for your roof and budget.
Physical samples against your actual exterior, not a screen.
Itemized by material and accessory so you can compare honestly.
Manufacturer-specified nailing, starter course, and ridge treatment.
What the shingle sits on and how the attic breathes both affect which product makes sense.
Magnet sweep, debris hauled, and a review of the finished roof with you.

options.d: Laminated construction, dimensional shadow line, and higher wind ratings than three-tab. The default recommendation for most homes here.
Tested to resist impact better than standard shingles. Higher material cost, and some insurers treat them differently — ask your carrier, not us, about premium implications.
Flat appearance and lower cost. Occasionally right for outbuildings or budget-constrained rentals.
Heavier laminated shingles that imitate slate or shake, for homes where the roof is a major part of the elevation.
Tear-resistant and far more stable underfoot than felt, and it holds up if weather arrives mid-job.
Self-adhering protection in the valleys and around every penetration, where the water actually concentrates.

benefits: Product guidance based on your roof, not on what is in the warehouse
Physical color samples against your actual exterior
Manufacturer-specified installation details
Straight talk about impact-resistant shingle trade-offs
localNote: Sun exposure in North Texas means the south and west slopes almost always show wear first, so any product comparison should be judged on those slopes rather than on the shaded north side of the house.

faqs.q: Are impact-resistant shingles worth it in DFW?
faqs.a: They can be, particularly if you have been hit more than once. They cost more and they are not indestructible. Some insurance carriers treat them differently — that is a question for your carrier, and we will not make claims about your premium.

faqs.q: Does shingle color affect my energy bill?
faqs.a: Color affects roof surface temperature, but attic insulation and ventilation have far more influence on what you actually pay. We would rather fix your ventilation than sell you a color story.

faqs.q: How many layers can a roof have?
faqs.a: We tear off rather than layer over, so this mostly matters for what we find during removal. Multiple existing layers add weight, hide deck problems, and increase disposal cost.

name: Storm Damage Roof Repair
title: Storm Damage Roof Repair in DFW | Timber Roofing
description: Storm damage roof repair and restoration across DFW. Documented post-storm inspections for hail, wind, leaks, and debris damage. Free inspections.
h1: Storm Damage Roof Repair and Restoration
heroSub: After a North Texas storm, the roofs that get handled well are the ones that got looked at properly first.
intro: Storm season here produces two problems at once: real damage, and a flood of out-of-town crews who follow the hail. Both need to be approached carefully. Damage should be documented before anybody starts talking about scope, and the company documenting it should still be reachable next year.
We inspect after storms, document what we find with photographs, explain the roofing scope in plain terms, and do the work. What we do not do is tell you what your insurance carrier will decide.

signs.d: Pieces of shingle or granule wash in the driveway after a storm mean the roof gave something up.
Soft metal shows hail impact clearly and is a good indicator to check the roof itself.
A crease across a shingle means it was bent back by wind and the seal is broken even if it laid back down.

signs.t: New interior stains after the storm
signs.d: The clearest sign of all, and the one that should be looked at first.
Hail is localized. If the street took a hit, your roof deserves a look.

causes.d: Impact bruising, granule loss, and fractured mat. The dominant storm damage type in this region.
Uplift along rakes, ridges, and edges, frequently ahead of the rain and often more damaging than the hail.
Water forced sideways under shingle edges and into wall transitions that would shed a normal rain fine.
Impact punctures and broken decking, especially under mature trees in older neighborhoods.

inspection: Post-storm assessment by a licensed inspector, slope by slope
Documentation of impact patterns, creasing, and granule loss with photographs
Check of soft metals — gutters, vents, flashing, screens — as corroborating evidence
Interior and attic check for active intrusion where accessible
Temporary protection recommendation if the roof is actively open

process.d: Active leaks and open roofs get prioritized.
Damage photographed and recorded, including date and location context.
We explain what is storm-related, what is wear, and what the repair scope would be.
Free written estimate describing the roofing work in specific terms.
Repair or replacement performed once scope is approved.
Cleanup, nail sweep, and a review of completed work with you.

options.d: Covering an actively open roof to limit further water damage while a permanent repair is scheduled.
Where damage is confined to specific slopes or details.
Where impact damage is widespread across the roof system.
Photographs and a written description of the roofing scope that you may share with your insurance carrier if you choose to.
Gutters, fascia, soffit, gable siding, and fencing handled alongside the roof rather than months later.
The most exposed lines on the roof, which take uplift first and are routinely skipped.

benefits: A licensed inspector documents the damage before any scope conversation
Photographs you keep, dated and organized
Local company you can still reach after the storm chasers leave
Clear separation between what is storm damage and what is normal wear
localNote: North Texas storms tend to arrive as fast-moving squall lines in spring, with wind out ahead and hail in the core. Damage is often patchy at the neighborhood level, which means your roof and the one across the street can end up in genuinely different condition after the same storm.

faqs.q: Do you handle the insurance claim for me?
faqs.a: No. We are roofers, not public adjusters, attorneys, or insurance representatives. We can document visible damage, explain the roofing scope, and provide project information that you may share with your carrier. Decisions about your claim rest between you and your insurer.

faqs.q: Should I get an inspection even without a leak?
faqs.a: Yes. Impact damage frequently does not leak immediately. It shortens the roof's life and shows up later, sometimes after the window to address it has closed.

faqs.q: How soon after a storm should I call?
faqs.a: Sooner is better, particularly if there is any sign of active intrusion. Documentation is also more useful when it is close in time to the event.

faqs.q: Why are there so many roofers knocking after a storm?
faqs.a: Because hail draws out-of-region crews. Ask anyone at your door who they are, where they are based, and whether they will be reachable in two years. That is a fair question and a good filter.

name: Hail Damage Roof Repair
title: Hail Damage Roof Repair in DFW | Timber Roofing
description: Hail damage roof inspection and repair across North Texas. Documented impact assessment by licensed inspectors, with free inspections and estimates.
heroSub: Hail damage rarely looks like a hole. It looks like a bruise, and it is easy to miss from the ground.
intro: North Texas sits in one of the most hail-prone regions in the United States. A single spring storm can put an entire neighborhood's roofs on a different timeline, and the damage frequently does not announce itself with a leak.

What hail actually does to an asphalt shingle is knock granules loose and fracture the mat underneath. The shingle keeps sitting there looking mostly fine while UV starts working on the exposed asphalt. That is why documented inspection after a hail event matters more than waiting to see if the ceiling stains.

signs.d: Round spots where granules were driven off, often soft to the touch. The classic hail signature on asphalt.
Hail damage is scattered and directional, not in the neat lines that wear or foot traffic produce.
Gutters, downspouts, roof vents, and AC fins dent visibly and are often the first confirmation.
A sudden heavy deposit after a storm means the roof surface took a beating.
Ridge and hip caps are more exposed and often show impact before field shingles do.

causes.d: Damage potential rises sharply with hailstone size, and dense stones do more than their diameter suggests.
Hail rarely falls straight down here. Slopes facing the storm take disproportionate damage.
An older, more brittle shingle fractures where a newer one might absorb the same impact.
Several moderate storms over consecutive seasons can add up to a failed roof.

inspection: Slope-by-slope impact assessment, since damage is directional
Test-square documentation approach to record impact density accurately
Soft-metal check on gutters, vents, and flashing as corroborating evidence
Ridge and hip cap inspection, where impact damage often shows first
Photographs of representative impacts with location context

process.d: Licensed inspector documents impact damage across every slope.
We show you the photographs and explain what we are seeing and why it matters.
A free estimate describing the roofing work in specific, itemized terms.
Performed once you approve the scope.
Full nail sweep and a walkthrough of completed work.
Gutters, vents, screens, and gable siding assessed as part of the same visit, since they took the same storm.

options.d: Where impact is genuinely confined to one or two elevations.
Where impact density across the roof makes repair impractical.
Class 4 products are worth discussing if you have been hit repeatedly. We will explain the trade-offs plainly.
Organized, dated photographs and a written roofing scope you may share with your carrier if you choose.
The most exposed line on the roof, and often the only part showing fracture.
Dented gutters, downspouts, and vent housings handled alongside the roof rather than months later.

benefits: Impact assessment by a licensed inspector rather than a driveway estimate
Documentation dated close to the storm event
Honest distinction between hail damage and ordinary aging
A local company still here for the next storm season
localNote: Hail swaths in the Metroplex are often only a few miles wide. Tarrant County can take a serious hit while Collin County stays dry, and within a single suburb the damage line can run down the middle of a street. Your neighbor's outcome is not evidence about your roof in either direction.

faqs.q: How do I know if my roof has hail damage?
faqs.a: Frequently you cannot tell from the ground, which is the entire problem. Dented gutters and vents are a strong hint. A free inspection settles it.

faqs.q: Will hail damage definitely leak?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, and not right away. Impact damage often shortens the roof's remaining life rather than opening it immediately. That delay is why so much hail damage goes unaddressed until it is too late to do much about it.

faqs.q: Can you tell me whether my claim will be approved?
faqs.a: No, and be cautious of anyone who says they can. We document visible damage and describe the roofing scope. Your carrier makes the decision.

faqs.q: How long do I have to deal with hail damage?
faqs.a: Policies and timelines vary, so check yours. From a purely roofing standpoint, sooner is better — exposed mat keeps degrading.

name: Wind Damage Roof Repair
title: Wind Damage Roof Repair in DFW | Timber Roofing
description: Wind damage roof repair across DFW — lifted and creased shingles, missing shingles, ridge and edge damage. Free inspections by licensed inspectors.
heroSub: A shingle that blew up and laid back down is still broken. The seal does not re-form.
intro: The wind out ahead of a North Texas squall line does damage that people consistently underestimate. Gusts get under the leading edge of a shingle, break the factory seal strip, and crease the shingle backward. Then it settles down again and looks fine from the driveway.
It is not fine. That shingle is no longer bonded, the crease is a fracture line, and the next storm will finish the job — usually taking the neighboring shingles with it.

signs.d: The obvious one. Also check the yard, the flower beds, and the neighbor's fence line.
A line across the shingle where it folded back. Reliable evidence of uplift even when nothing is missing.
Edges and peaks catch the most uplift force and fail first.
Shingles that can be lifted by hand with no resistance have lost their seal.
Metal that has been peeled or bent back opens a direct path for water.

causes.d: The dominant wind damage mechanism here, often ahead of a fast-moving line of storms.
Once the adhesive bond fails, wind resistance drops sharply for the rest of that shingle's life.
Uplift pressure is highest at roof edges and corners, which is exactly where installation shortcuts show up.
Heat and UV weaken seal strips over time, so an older roof gives up in winds a newer one would shrug off.

inspection: Check windward slopes first, since wind damage is strongly directional
Inspect rakes, ridges, hips, and eaves where uplift concentrates
Hand-test seal integrity on representative shingles
Look for creasing on shingles that appear intact from a distance
Check flashing, drip edge, and ridge caps for displacement

We show you what is unsealed or creased, not just what is missing.
Free and itemized.
Damaged shingles replaced and properly sealed, flashing and edge metal addressed.
Debris removed, magnet sweep, walkthrough.
We hand-test the repaired area and the courses around it, because a shingle that is down is not necessarily a shingle that is bonded.

Rebuilding the most exposed line on the roof.

options.t: Edge metal and drip edge repair
options.d: Re-securing or replacing peeled metal at rakes and eaves.
Where uplift damage is widespread or the roof was already near the end.
Re-establishing the starter strip at eaves and rakes where uplift pressure is highest and it is most often missing.
Where creasing and broken seals run across an entire elevation, replacing that slope rather than chasing individual shingles.

benefits: Creased-but-present shingles identified, not just missing ones
Directional inspection that reflects how wind actually damages a roof
Photographic evidence of unsealed shingles
Repairs that re-establish the seal rather than face-nailing
localNote: Spring squall lines move through the Metroplex fast and hit the west and south elevations hardest. In older neighborhoods with mature trees, wind damage and limb impact frequently arrive together on the same roof.

faqs.q: A few shingles blew off. Is that a whole-roof problem?
faqs.a: Not automatically. But shingles rarely leave alone — the surrounding ones usually lost their seal too. An inspection will tell you how far the unsealed area extends.

faqs.q: Can wind damage a roof without removing shingles?
faqs.a: Yes, and this is the part most homeowners miss. Creased and unsealed shingles are damaged shingles even when every one of them is still on the roof.

faqs.q: How fast do winds need to be to cause damage?
faqs.a: Less than people expect, particularly on older roofs with weakened seal strips or on roofs where the original nailing pattern was wrong.

name: Roof Leak Repair
title: Roof Leak Repair in Dallas–Fort Worth | Timber Roofing
description: Roof leak diagnosis and repair across DFW and North Texas. We trace the leak to its actual source rather than patching where the stain is.
h1: Roof Leak Repair and Leak Diagnosis
heroSub: Water enters in one place and shows up in another. Finding the first place is the whole job.
intro: A ceiling stain is evidence, not a location. Water gets in at a failed detail, runs down the underside of the decking or along a rafter, and drops through the drywall wherever gravity and insulation decide. Repairs aimed at the stain are how leaks come back.
Most leaks in North Texas homes come from a short list: pipe boots, chimney and wall flashing, valleys, skylights, and shingles that lost their seal in a wind event. We work that list systematically.

signs.d: Especially rings that darken or expand after rain.
Often visible before anything shows on the ceiling below.

signs.t: A musty smell in the attic or upstairs
signs.d: Chronic slow leaks announce themselves by smell before they show themselves.

signs.t: Peeling paint near a chimney or wall line
signs.d: Frequently a flashing failure rather than a roof-surface problem.

signs.t: Drips only in heavy or wind-driven rain
signs.d: A classic sign of a marginal detail that sheds normal rain and fails under sideways water.

causes.d: Cracked rubber collars around plumbing vents. Extremely common on Texas roofs after a decade of UV.
Wall, chimney, and skylight flashing that was sealed instead of replaced during a previous repair.
Valleys carry concentrated water and clog with leaves, then back water up under the shingles.
Wind-driven rain gets under shingles that no longer bond.
Overflowing gutters push water back onto the fascia and roof edge instead of away from it.

inspection: Start inside — interior evidence, then attic, tracing the water path upward
Identify the entry point on the roof rather than the nearest visible defect
Inspect all penetrations, flashing, and valleys in the water path
Assess how far damage extends into decking and insulation
Photograph the source so you can see the actual cause

process.d: Interior, attic, and roof review to find the real entry point.
We show you where the water is getting in and why.
Free, scoped to the actual fix.
Replace the failed component and rebuild the detail correctly.
Completed repair photographed and reviewed with you.
We tell you what to watch for on the ceiling over the next few weeks and what would mean calling us back.

options.d: New boot correctly integrated into the shingle courses rather than caulked over.
New step and counter flashing at walls and chimneys.
Stripping back and rebuilding the valley with proper underlayment.
Where chronic leaking has already softened the sheathing.
Replacing the flashing kit rather than caulking the glass, which is where these usually get patched badly.
Clearing or resizing gutters where the leak turns out to be water backing up over the roof edge.

benefits: Diagnosis before pricing, so the repair addresses the real source
Photos of the entry point, not just of the finished work
Honest assessment of whether surrounding damage needs attention too
Small leak jobs treated seriously
localNote: Long dry stretches followed by intense rainfall are hard on North Texas roofs. Sealants shrink and crack in the heat, then the first heavy storm of the season finds every one of those cracks at once. That is why so many leaks around here appear suddenly rather than gradually.

faqs.q: Can you find a leak that only happens sometimes?
faqs.a: Usually. Intermittent leaks almost always point to a wind-driven-rain path or a marginal flashing detail, and both leave physical evidence in the attic even when they are not actively dripping.

faqs.q: Should I put a bucket under it and wait?
faqs.a: For a night, sure. Longer than that and you are letting the water do damage to insulation, framing, and drywall that costs far more than the roofing repair.

faqs.q: Does a leak mean I need a new roof?
faqs.a: Often not. A single failed detail on an otherwise sound roof is a repair. We will tell you which situation you are in.

faqs.q: What if the leak is not from the roof at all?
faqs.a: It happens — HVAC condensate lines, plumbing, and window flashing all get blamed on roofs. If that is what we find, we will tell you, and we are not going to sell you roofing work you do not need.

We inspect, document, and explain. We do not decide what your insurance carrier will do, and we will not pretend otherwise to get you to sign something.

signs.d: Even moderate hail is worth a look, particularly on a roof over ten years old.

signs.d: Wind damage is easy to miss and does not require anything to be visibly missing.

Documentation closest to the event is the most useful documentation.
Storm damage frequently does not leak until months later, by which point the connection is harder to establish.

Photographic record of impacts, creasing, and displacement

Seal integrity and creasing on windward elevations.
Punctures and structural damage from limbs or airborne material.

A documented condition record before storm season, so afterwards there is something to compare against.
Roof condition documented ahead of a sale or purchase, where it tends to move negotiations.

Performed by licensed inspectors
Dated photographs you keep
Honest separation of storm damage from ordinary wear
localNote: Because Metroplex hail swaths are narrow and erratic, damage assessment has to be property-specific. Regional storm reports are a starting point, not a substitute for somebody looking at your particular roof.

faqs.q: Should I get inspected if my neighbor's roof was approved?
faqs.a: It is a reasonable prompt to get looked at, but it proves nothing about your roof. Hail is patchy enough that adjacent houses genuinely differ.

faqs.q: Do you charge for a post-storm inspection?
faqs.a: No. Free inspections, free estimates.

faqs.q: What if you find nothing?
faqs.a: Then we tell you that and you have documentation showing your roof was in good condition on that date. That is a useful thing to have.

name: Emergency Roof Tarping
title: Emergency Roof Tarping in DFW | Timber Roofing
description: Temporary emergency roof protection across North Texas to limit water damage after storm damage, while a permanent repair is scheduled.
h1: Emergency Roof Tarping and Temporary Protection
heroSub: When a roof is open, the priority is stopping water from doing more damage than the storm did.
intro: Temporary protection is exactly that — a controlled way to keep water out of an open roof until a proper repair can be scheduled and performed. It is not a repair, and anyone who treats it as one is doing you a disservice.
The value of good temporary protection is measured in what it prevents: soaked insulation, ruined drywall, damaged flooring, and the mold problem that follows all three in a hot Texas attic.

signs.d: Water coming through a ceiling during or after a storm needs to be stopped from above.
Impact from a limb or airborne debris that has opened the roof.
Exposed underlayment or bare deck will not survive the next rain.
The gap between one storm and the next is when protection matters most.

causes.d: The most common cause of a genuinely open roof in North Texas.
Large areas of shingles and underlayment stripped away in a single event.
Damage that has compromised decking or framing.

Determine the safe extent of temporary protection

Secure covering installed to shed water away from the opening.
Photographs of the damage and the temporary work.

Documented with photographs

Clear about what temporary protection is and is not
localNote: Spring storms in North Texas often arrive in sequence, with a second round hours or days behind the first. That gap is exactly when an open roof turns a repair into a renovation.

faqs.q: How long can temporary protection stay on?
faqs.a: It is a short-term measure. Sun, wind, and heat degrade any temporary covering, and it should be replaced by a permanent repair as soon as practical.

faqs.q: Is emergency protection free?
faqs.a: The inspection is free. Temporary protection is work, and it will be quoted before we do it.

faqs.q: What should I do inside while I wait?
faqs.a: Move what you can out of the water's path, contain drips, and photograph everything. Do not stand under a bulging ceiling.

Maintenance is not glamorous and it is not a big invoice, which is exactly why so many roofing companies do not bother offering it.

A displaced shingle or lifted flashing detail can sit unnoticed for years.

faqs.q: How often should a roof be inspected?
faqs.a: Once a year is a reasonable baseline, plus after any significant hail or wind event.

faqs.q: Is maintenance worth it on a newer roof?
faqs.a: Yes, mostly for the penetrations and drainage. A new roof does not mean new pipe boots stay flexible forever in this heat.

name: Roof Ventilation

description: Roof ventilation assessment and correction for DFW homes. Balanced intake and exhaust to protect shingles, decking, and attic conditions.
heroSub: A roof that cannot breathe cooks itself from the inside, and the damage shows up as a shingle problem.
intro: Ventilation is the part of the roof system homeowners hear about least and pay for most. Attic air in a Texas summer gets extraordinarily hot, and without balanced intake and exhaust that heat sits against the underside of the decking all day.

The result is shingles aging faster than they should, higher cooling load, and in some cases moisture problems in winter. Ventilation is also one of the more common conditions attached to manufacturer material coverage.

signs.t: An attic that is brutally hot
signs.d: Some heat is expected. Air that feels like an oven late in the day usually means exhaust is not keeping up.
Especially over sections of the attic with poor airflow.

signs.t: Condensation or rusted fasteners in the attic
signs.d: Moisture is not leaving the space.
Insulation pushed into the eaves is the single most common intake problem we find.

causes.d: Too few vents, or vents sized for a smaller attic than the one they are serving.
Exhaust cannot work without intake. Soffit blockage defeats the whole system.
Combining incompatible exhaust types can short-circuit airflow so the attic pulls from the wrong place.
New rooflines frequently disrupt an attic's original ventilation path.

inspection: Measure or estimate attic area against existing vent capacity
Check intake at soffits and eaves for blockage
Identify mixed or conflicting exhaust types
Look for heat and moisture evidence on decking and framing
Recommend a balanced correction rather than simply adding vents

process.d: Intake and exhaust evaluated together, not separately.
A balanced plan with reasoning you can follow.
Free and itemized.
Corrections made, typically alongside roofing work where practical.
Clearing or adding soffit intake first, because exhaust cannot work without it.
A second look at the attic once the corrections are in, to confirm air is actually moving.

options.d: Continuous exhaust along the ridge line, generally the most even distribution when intake supports it.
Individual roof vents placed for coverage.
Wind-driven exhaust, still common across North Texas neighborhoods.
Clearing or adding soffit intake so exhaust can actually function.
Adding intake where an eave has none, which is more common than most homeowners expect.
Keeping insulation out of the eaves so the intake path stays open.

benefits: Intake and exhaust assessed as one system
Shingle life protected from the underside
Attic moisture and heat conditions addressed
Corrections that meet manufacturer installation requirements
localNote: North Texas attics routinely run far above outdoor temperature on summer afternoons. Ventilation here is less about winter moisture than about getting relentless summer heat out from under the deck.

faqs.q: Will more vents fix my hot attic?
faqs.a: Only if intake supports them. Adding exhaust without intake can actually make airflow worse by pulling conditioned air from the house.

faqs.q: Can ventilation affect my shingle coverage?
faqs.a: Manufacturer requirements commonly include ventilation criteria. We install to those requirements and we will not make claims about your specific warranty terms — read the product documentation.

name: Roof Flashing Repair
title: Roof Flashing Repair in DFW | Timber Roofing
description: Flashing repair and replacement for North Texas homes — wall, chimney, valley, and skylight flashing rebuilt correctly rather than sealed over.
heroSub: Roofs mostly do not leak in the middle. They leak where the roof meets something else.
intro: Flashing is the metal that manages every transition on a roof — where it meets a wall, a chimney, a skylight, or another roof plane. It is where water is most concentrated and where installation quality shows most clearly.
The most common flashing 'repair' we find on North Texas homes is a bead of sealant smeared over the problem. That buys a season or two. Rebuilding the detail correctly fixes it.

signs.t: Stains on walls below a roof line
signs.d: Especially where a second story meets a lower roof.
Visible corrosion or metal pulling away from the wall or chimney.

signs.t: Visible caulk as the primary seal
signs.d: Sealant should supplement flashing, not replace it.

signs.t: Leaks near a chimney or skylight
signs.d: These two locations account for a disproportionate share of roof leaks.

causes.d: Caulk shrinks and cracks in Texas heat, usually within a few seasons.
Old flashing left in place to save cost during a previous re-roof.
Chimney and brick movement opens counter-flashing joints over time.
Flashing installed over rather than woven into the shingle courses.

Check counter-flashing embedment in masonry
Look for sealant used as a primary seal
Assess whether surrounding shingles must be disturbed for a correct repair
Photograph the failure for you

New flashing installed and correctly integrated with the roof covering.
Completed work photographed and reviewed.
The surrounding courses rebuilt over the new metal, since flashing is layered into the roof rather than laid on it.

Metal set into masonry above step flashing, typical at chimneys.
Where a roof plane terminates into a vertical wall.
Open or closed valley treatment rebuilt properly.
A small saddle diverting water around the uphill side of a wide chimney, and a frequent omission on North Texas homes.
The small piece at the bottom of a roof-to-wall run that keeps water out of the wall cavity.

Correct layering with the shingle courses

Honest scope, including the shingle work a real repair requires
localNote: Brick and stone are everywhere in North Texas residential construction, which means chimney and wall transitions are extremely common leak points — and masonry movement in expansive clay soils keeps reopening those joints.

faqs.q: Can flashing just be resealed?
faqs.a: Sometimes as a short-term measure. If the metal is corroded, displaced, or was installed incorrectly, sealant is a delay rather than a repair.

faqs.q: Why does flashing repair require removing shingles?
faqs.a: Because flashing is layered into the shingle courses. Doing it right means disturbing the surrounding area, and any quote that does not account for that is not describing a real repair.

name: Chimney and Roof Penetration Repair

intro: Plumbing vents, exhaust vents, chimneys, skylights, satellite mounts, and solar attachments all break the roof plane. Each one depends on a detail doing its job, and each one ages differently than the shingles around it.

Pipe boots in particular are the single most under-appreciated failure point on a Texas roof. The rubber collar cracks in UV years before the shingles are finished, and it is a small, inexpensive fix that prevents a large, expensive one.

signs.t: Cracked rubber around a vent pipe
signs.d: Visible splitting on the collar. Extremely common after eight to twelve Texas summers.
A ceiling stain near a bathroom or kitchen vent stack points straight at the boot.
Metal vent covers that have corroded or lifted.
Daylight or open joints where the chimney meets the roof.

Metal and masonry expand and contract at different rates and eventually open the joint.
Old satellite mounts and removed vents left improperly sealed.
Boots installed on top of shingles instead of layered into them.

inspection: Inspect every penetration on the roof individually
Check boot flexibility and collar integrity
Assess chimney flashing and cricket where present
Identify abandoned or improperly sealed penetrations
Photograph each problem area

Free, itemized by component.

Completed work reviewed with you.

Step and counter flashing, plus a cricket where the chimney width warrants one.

localNote: Wide masonry chimneys are common on North Texas homes, and any chimney over about thirty inches across on the upslope side generally needs a cricket to divert water around it. Missing crickets are a recurring cause of chronic chimney leaks in this market.

faqs.q: How long do pipe boots last in Texas?
faqs.a: Frequently less than the shingles around them. UV exposure cracks the rubber, and replacing a few boots is one of the highest-value small repairs on a roof here.

faqs.q: Do you repair chimneys themselves?
faqs.a: We handle the roofing side — flashing, crickets, and the roof-to-chimney transition. Masonry repair, crown work, and flue issues belong to a chimney specialist and we will tell you when that is what you need.

name: New Construction Roofing
title: New Construction Roofing in DFW | Timber Roofing
description: Roofing for new residential construction and additions across DFW — coordinated scheduling, correct detailing, and inspection-ready installation.
heroSub: The roof that goes on a new build sets the clock for everything that follows it.
intro: New construction roofing is a scheduling problem as much as a roofing problem. Dry-in has to happen at the right moment, and the finished roof has to be coordinated with framing, mechanical penetrations, and the rest of the exterior trades.
The details that get skipped on new builds — valley protection, correct nailing, real flashing at wall transitions, balanced ventilation — are the ones that produce a leaking six-year-old roof.

signs.d: Custom home or infill construction needing a full roof system.
New rooflines that must tie into existing ones correctly.
Garages, shops, and covered outdoor structures.

causes.d: Roofing gets compressed when earlier trades run late, and details are the first thing sacrificed.
Where new roof meets existing roof is the highest-risk detail on any addition.
Mechanical and plumbing penetrations added after the roof is on, without proper flashing.

inspection: Review plans and roof geometry before scheduling
Confirm ventilation approach for the finished attic volume
Identify tie-in points and detail them deliberately
Coordinate dry-in timing with the build schedule

process.d: Scope and materials confirmed against the drawings.
Weather protection installed at the right point in the build.
Underlayment, flashing, ventilation, and roof covering.
Penetrations flashed properly as other trades complete their work.
Walkthrough with the builder or homeowner.
Intake and exhaust confirmed against the finished attic volume rather than the plan set.

options.d: The standard for most new North Texas residential construction.
Worth considering at build time, when the cost delta is smallest.
New-to-existing transitions detailed and flashed properly.
Weather protection installed at the right point in the build, with the finished roof scheduled separately.
Garages, shops, and covered outdoor structures roofed to match the main house.
A balanced intake and exhaust plan specified for the finished structure rather than added afterwards.

benefits: Details handled deliberately rather than under schedule pressure
Ventilation designed for the finished structure
Tie-ins treated as the critical detail they are
One point of contact for the roof scope
localNote: North Texas has had sustained residential construction for two decades, and the roofs installed fastest during the biggest booms are frequently the ones we are called back to look at first.

faqs.q: Do you work with builders and general contractors?
faqs.a: Contact us with the project details and schedule. Fit depends on scope, timeline, and location.

faqs.q: Can you roof an addition to match my existing roof?
faqs.a: We will match as closely as the current product line allows and be direct with you about how well a weathered existing roof will match new material.
